provenance: User-requested nine deployment/operations topics, tailored against the same-repository source snapshot.
counting: Nine shared requirements projected by product. Product projections are not additive top-level features. Preserve all existing feature counts, IDs, states and evidence.
existing_records_policy: Existing catalogs, IDs, owners, status, acceptance, history and feature counts are unchanged. These projections are supplemental delivery/qualification refinements.
product_boundary: This repository implements diagnostic utilities and a scaffold for future infrastructure contracts. No Terraform resources, Ansible deployment or product runtime exists here. constraints: Source these requirements from the user's nine requested topics and same-repository records. Do not copy private code findings or operational details from another repository.

Tailor scope and acceptance to the local product. Native Slurm/head-node/compute administration belongs to HPC. Grid Engine retains its native scheduler. Other products document external integration only if explicitly selected and justified.
Map to existing local backlog IDs and source/doc paths. Where no canonical catalog exists, say so and use existing repository references; do not invent parent IDs.

Keep existing canonical feature IDs/counts, statuses, owners, historical evidence and issue states unchanged. This is a supplemental planned backlog; no implementation, native/site acceptance, HA, security, recovery or production readiness claim.

Use self-hosted, existing user-controlled infrastructure and existing free tools; preserve current PostgreSQL and storage choices per product. No paid services, new runtime dependencies or default cloud provisioning.

Keep shared nine IDs across product projections and use AC suffixes -AC1..-AC5. Criteria may be adapted to the product but Markdown and JSON must match exactly. Use all 45 IDs and record applicability explicitly.

Acceptance status stays Not run. Owners are proposed roles, with assignment pending. Planned per-repository docs/checklists do not authorize destructive installation, disk erasure, deployment or automated remediation.

Worksheets must use unfilled fields (TBD), secret references instead of secret values, and blank evidence/signoff. Never invent actual addresses, hardware, site names, credentials, deployment dates or measured RTO/RPO.
Update an existing backlog index or README with links and a truthful scope/count summary. Update any required documentation inventory without rewriting historical/canonical source copies.
Native acceptance and evidence for original requirements remain separate. Close documentation PR after eligible merge, not unfinished product acceptance issues.

requirements.scope: Plan supported product roles, control/data paths, capacity and prerequisites, and separate source capability from installed readiness.

acceptance.text: Record the intended topology, role boundaries, supported operating systems and hardware, storage/data ownership, environment limits and product-specific exclusions in a versioned architecture worksheet.
Record measurable capacity, latency, throughput, concurrency and resource budgets plus workload assumptions before tuning or acceptance; retain baseline evidence and avoid invented measurements.

Validate prerequisite identity, DNS/time synchronization, storage capacity, network access, package/driver rights, dependencies and operator authority; fail readiness for missing or inconsistent inputs.

Map each installation and operational capability to its existing backlog parent, Terraform/OpenTofu or infrastructure contract, Ansible or configuration contract, and required source/native/site evidence.
Record proposed delivery/operations owners, unresolved decisions, dependency order, change window and explicit review gates; a missing approval or failed prerequisite keeps readiness blocked.

acceptance.text: Complete an IPAM worksheet for each applicable interface or virtual endpoint with role, hostname, address family/prefix, subnet, gateway, VLAN, DNS, reservation method and owner; reserve virtual and provisioning addresses separately.
Validate address/prefix syntax, subnet and pool overlap, duplicate addresses, static/DHCP exclusions, routing and capacity; use actual site allocations only after operator review.
Define required inbound/outbound ports, trust zones, administrative access, routing, DNS and time dependencies; deny unrelated traffic and keep out-of-band management isolated where present.

Validate connectivity, name resolution, configured MTU and relevant throughput/latency between each required role, including failure and rollback behavior, without exposing private endpoint values in diagnostic evidence.
Version and review address changes, VIP moves and firewall/routing updates; prove conflict detection and rollback before any live allocation, and record unsupported address families explicitly.

requirements.title: High availability

acceptance.text: Declare supported single-instance, active/passive or active/active topology and each stateful dependency; where HA is unsupported, record the limitation and operator-approved recovery approach.

Only for a separately approved HA design, specify leadership/quorum, fencing or equivalent ownership exclusion, endpoint movement and data consistency. Otherwise record why these mechanisms are not applicable to the selected topology; no HA pass is implied.
Set reviewed RTO, RPO and workload/session safety requirements before trials; define how progress, jobs, commands and durable state survive a role or dependency failure.

For the supported single-host/package topology, inject process and host/dependency outages and measure isolated restoration and state/permission outcomes against predeclared objectives; do not label restoration as HA failover.

Exercise return to the last qualified single-host/package configuration and verify ownership and unresolved incidents. Record native HA as not applicable with its reason; future HA requires a separately approved design and trials.

requirements.title: Slurm validation
requirements.owner_role: HPC scheduler owner or selected integration owner
requirements.scope: HPC owns native Slurm acceptance. Other products mark native Slurm administration out of scope; qualify only an explicitly selected external adapter. Never replace Grid Engine's scheduler.

acceptance.text: Record native Slurm administration as not applicable to this product, with the product-specific reason and current execution authority. External Slurm integration is opt-in and requires an approved design before adding an adapter.

If an external Slurm integration is explicitly selected and approved: For applicable native or integration targets, verify exact scheduler/configuration identity, authentication, node/partition visibility, accounting dependencies and current health; stale or simulated observations cannot satisfy native readiness. Otherwise retain a justified not-applicable disposition; do not report native scheduler trials as passed.

If an external Slurm integration is explicitly selected and approved: Exercise authorized CPU and, where supported, GPU/GRES job submission, resource/account/QoS limits, isolation, accounting and completion on the actual target; record unsupported cases explicitly. Otherwise retain a justified not-applicable disposition; do not report native scheduler trials as passed.

If an external Slurm integration is explicitly selected and approved: Exercise unauthorized requests, node drain/rejoin, controller or adapter interruption, timeout/cancellation and recovery while preserving active jobs, ownership and bounded diagnostics. Otherwise retain a justified not-applicable disposition; do not report native scheduler trials as passed.

If an external Slurm integration is explicitly selected and approved: Measure applicable submission/status/accounting latency and load/soak behavior against predeclared budgets, retain revision/environment-bound evidence, and leave native acceptance open until those trials pass. Otherwise retain a justified not-applicable disposition; do not report native scheduler trials as passed.

requirements.title: Security hardening
requirements.scope: Qualify the existing local trust boundaries and product-specific access/privacy protections without weakening supported behavior or adding a new security service.

acceptance.text: Document a threat and trust-boundary review for installation, administration, application traffic, stored data, agents/workers and dependencies; map findings to existing security requirements and assigned remediation roles.

Qualify least-privilege service identities, administrative authentication, role/tenant or device scope, secure remote access, certificate/key lifecycle and secret-reference handling on the supported installation.

Apply reviewed host/service hardening and minimal network exposure using existing configuration ownership; verify updates, dependency provenance and relevant vulnerability/secret checks without disabling required protections.

Exercise denied access, revoked credentials/certificates, unauthorized configuration, malformed inputs and private-data redaction; diagnostics must remain bounded and must not contain secrets or customer payloads.
Record hardening profile identity, evidence, residual exceptions, accountable approval and remediation expiry; failed checks or unapproved exceptions block go-live.
